How would you use your platform as a New York State Legislator to advocate for protection of LGBTQ people across the city, state and country? Unlike legislators in other states, I will not allow New York to succumb to regressive policies. As a Senator I have passed legislation to end conversion therapy, because I understand the importance of keeping our LGBTQ youth protected. The LGBTQ community has historically been over policed, and research shows that law enforcement continues to disproportionately target marginalized people: What do you view as the New York State Legislatures role in ensuring law enforcement oversight, funding, and the needs of marginalized communities? At the Senate I currently have legislation like “The Keep Police Radio Public Act,” which allows for public oversight of communications. 2

[PDF page 3] 2024 New York State Endorsement Questionnaire Michael Gianaris New York State Senate 12 New York State is experiencing a housing crisis and the LGBTQ community disproportionately experiences homelessness, especially our LGBTQ youth and seniors. How do we ensure that any plan is equitable to the LGBTQ Community and other marginalized groups? In 2019, I helped to pass some of the most expansive tenant protections across the country, and continue to fight to do so. This year, I helped to further those reforms by enacting Good Cause Eviction protection, which is the strongest anti-eviction law in state history. Much of the work I do remains focused on protecting our most vulnerable populations, and that includes fighting for equitable and accessible housing opportunities. With the repeal of Roe V. Wade and state legislatures across the country implementing abortion bans, New York State has become a safe haven for reproductive rights. In today’s political landscape, what do you see as the New York Legislature’s role in protecting and expanding reproductive healthcare? The decision to overturn Roe v Wade attacked what has been a fundamental right for Americans for the last half-century and profoundly reversed so much progress that has been made for health and economic equity. As part of the Senate Majority, I helped to enshrine Roe v Wade and keep reproductive health care accessible for New Yorkers. Our hope is that by investing in public education, we can foster a new generation of thinkers that adopt more diverse and accepting mindsets. Finally, we hope to increase public safety during our next term in oVice. This will extend to all New Yorkers and hopefully help the LGBTQ community feel safe from discrimination.. I hope that these common sense solutions, although broad, will aid the LGBTQ community for years to come.
